speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with a neck swelling; to help me understand your condition, please tell me how long you have noticed this lump and if it has changed in size recently. Are you experiencing any pain, difficulty swallowing, or changes in your voice?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Squamous Cell Carcinoma to a cervical lymph node (likely from head and neck primary) or metastatic adenocarcinoma from colon cancer. Given the history of colon cancer, a metastatic deposit or a new primary malignancy is the leading concern. I need to perform a fine-needle aspiration of the neck mass and obtain imaging to determine the origin. REQUEST TEST: Fine_Needle_Aspiration; REQUEST TEST: CT_Neck_Chest_Abel
